P1_fx_receipts.question: Can resident individuals receive foreign currency for services or digital exports? Any conversion or repatriation rule?
P1_fx_receipts.answer: Yes, but foreign currency must be surrendered. Niger left ECOWAS in 2025 but, per secondary reports, remains in the UEMOA/BCEAO CFA-franc union. Under Regulation 06/2024/CM/UEMOA, residents must surrender all foreign-currency income received outside the UEMOA or paid by a non-resident to an approved intermediary (art. 5), and repatriate all export proceeds for goods and services (art. 11).

sources.title: Règlement 06/2024/CM/UEMOA, art. 5
sources.quote: Les résidents sont tenus de céder à un intermédiaire agréé tous les revenus ou produits en devises encaissés en dehors de l'UEMOA ou versés par un non-résident.

sources.title: Règlement 06/2024, art. 11
sources.quote: Les opérateurs économiques résidents sont tenus d'encaisser et de rapatrier dans le pays d’exportation, auprès d'un intermédiaire agréé, l’intégralité des sommes provenant des exportations de biens et services à l’étranger

P1_fx_receipts.notes: AES states' continued UEMOA membership rests on secondary reports; re-check.

P2_fcy_account.question: Can resident individuals hold a foreign-currency account locally?
P2_fcy_account.answer: Only with authorisation from the Minister of Finance after a binding BCEAO opinion (UEMOA Reg. 06/2024 art. 7).

sources.title: Règlement 06/2024, art. 7
sources.quote: Article 7 : Détention de comptes en devises par les résidents L’ouverture par les résidents de comptes intérieurs en devises ou de comptes à l'étranger est soumise à l'autorisation préalable du Ministre chargé des Finances, après avis conforme de la BCEAO

P3_local_gateways.question: Which local payment gateways can an individual or sole trader use to accept online payments?
P3_local_gateways.answer: Global platform availability for Niger (automated collector snapshots, Oct 2026). Available: Paddle (not on its exclusion list; software sellers only, each seller reviewed); Lemon Squeezy (bank payouts); Polar (payouts); Whop (payouts); Dodo Payments (sellers); Google Play (developer registration). Not listed: Stripe (merchant sign-up); Etsy seller payments; YouTube Partner Program.

L1_registration.question: Must an individual register a business to sell digital services/products? Simplest legal form?
L1_registration.answer: Simplest: the OHADA entreprenant / individual enterprise, registered at the Maison de l'Entreprise one-stop shop in Niamey, which delivers the RCCM and NIF. A commercial guide estimates FCFA 30,000–60,000 and about 72 hours.

L2_tax_id.answer: The NIF (numéro d'identification fiscale), delivered with RCCM registration at the Maison de l'Entreprise per a commercial guide. No official source was captured.

L3_income_tax_foreign.question: Income tax on foreign-source income for residents; rates or special regimes
L3_income_tax_foreign.answer: The impôt synthétique applies to individuals in activities subject to the profits tax (ISB) with turnover incl. tax under FCFA 50m. Since Finance Law 2025, the 2-year exemption for newly registered synthetic-regime businesses is repealed, so no exemption applies on creation. Rates and the treatment of foreign-source income were not established.

sources.publisher: Chambre de Commerce et d'Industrie du Niger
sources.title: Commentaires sur les nouvelles dispositions de la Loi de Finances pour 2025
sources.quote: Il convient de rappeler que l’impôt synthétique s’applique aux personnes physiques qui exercent une activité soumise à l’ISB et qui réalise un chiffre d’affaires TTC inférieur à 50 millions FCFA.

sources.title: LF 2025 — exemption repealed
sources.quote: Ainsi donc, aucune exonération de l’impôt synthétique n’est accordée à la création de l’entreprise.

sources.quote: la suppression de l'exonération de deux (2) ans accordée aux nouvelles entreprises immatriculées sous le régime de l'impôt synthétique », indique le communiqué .

L4_vat_gst.question: VAT/GST: rate, registration threshold, treatment of exported digital services
L4_vat_gst.answer: VAT is 19% (single rate per a 2011 official overview; a 5% reduced rate exists for some staples per other sources). Since Finance Law 2025, sales and services made in Niger through foreign or local e-commerce platforms, and platform commissions, are subject to VAT. The treatment of exported services and the registration threshold were not established.

sources.publisher: République du Niger — overview of the tax system in force (2011), hosted by UN FfD
sources.title: Système fiscal en vigueur 2011
sources.quote: Le taux de la TVA, actuellement en vigueur, est de 19%.

sources.publisher: Chambre de Commerce et d'Industrie du Niger
sources.title: LF 2025 — VAT on e-commerce platforms
sources.quote: La loi de finances pour 2025 a élargi les opérations imposables à la TVA aux ventes de biens et les prest ations de services effectuées au Niger à travers les plateformes de commerce électronique étrangères ou locales ainsi que les commissions que ces opérateurs des plateformes auront perçues.

L4_vat_gst.notes: The 19% figure comes from a 2011 document; not re-confirmed against the current CGI.

L5_data_protection.question: Data-protection law applicable to a small online business
L5_data_protection.answer: Law 2022-59 of 16 Dec 2022 (amended by Law 2023-31 and 2024 ordinances) replaced Law 2017-28. The HAPDP is the independent authority, attached to the Presidency. Processing personal data requires prior notification to the HAPDP, which is not required if a data protection officer is appointed, except for cross-border transfers. Controllers also file an annual report (art. 64).

sources.publisher: République du Niger — Loi n° 2023-31 (copy hosted by DataGuidance)
sources.title: Loi n° 2023-31 modifiant la loi n° 2022-59
sources.quote: La HAPDP est une autorité administrative indépendante chargée de veiller à la conformité des traitements des données à caractère personnel aux dispositions des textes en vigueur et des conventions internationales auxquelles le Niger est partie.

sources.title: Data Protection in Niger
sources.quote: The processing of personal data is subject to prior notification to the HAPD. If a data controller appoints a data protection officer, notification is unnecessary unless personal data is being transferred across national borders.

L5_data_protection.notes: TRAP: several compliance sites still cite Law 2017-28 as current. hapdp.ne returned a TLS hostname mismatch (blocked, not bypassed).

L6_consumer_ecommerce.question: Consumer-protection / e-commerce rules for online sales (refunds, disclosures)
L6_consumer_ecommerce.answer: Law 2019-03 of 30 April 2019 on electronic transactions governs e-commerce. Its consumer withdrawal and disclosure provisions were not read.
L6_consumer_ecommerce.note: Searched 2026-10-20: 'Niger loi transactions électroniques 2019 droit de rétractation consommateur'. Found only a Council of Europe webinar slide naming Law 2019-03; the law text was not located.

L7_incentives.question: Legal incentives / tax holidays / special zones relevant to small digital businesses
L7_incentives.answer: No current small-business tax holiday: the 2-year synthetic-tax exemption for new businesses was repealed by Finance Law 2025. The synthetic regime (turnover under FCFA 50m) remains the simplified option (L3).

D1_id_document.question: Identity documents residents use for KYC (gateways, banks, platforms)
D1_id_document.answer: The national identity card. Niger launched enrolment for the AES biometric national identity card in Niamey on 27 March 2026 (pilot phase, then progressive national rollout). Fingerprints, facial photo and electronic signature are captured.

W1_workarounds.question: Simple, legal routes around payment barriers for a beginner (no misrepresentation, nominees or sanctions evasion)
W1_workarounds.answer: Barriers: Stripe does not accept merchants here; platforms that pay out through PayPal Payouts cannot pay PayPal accounts here (not on PayPal's Payouts list, see P4 for ordinary PayPal receiving); Wise does not let residents hold money. Simple legal routes: (1) Sell digital products or software through a merchant of record: Paddle (software/SaaS only; each seller reviewed), Lemon Squeezy (bank payouts), Polar, Dodo Payments. The platform is the legal seller to your customers, handles card payments and consumer VAT/sales tax, and pays you out. You still declare the payouts as your income at home (see L3). (2) Sell services on Upwork, which is available here (not on its restricted list). Which withdrawal methods you get (bank, PayPal, Payoneer, etc.) depends on the country and shows in your account. (3) Paid apps and in-app sales through Google Play (merchant registration available here). (4) For direct clients, a bank transfer (SWIFT) into your own local account always works. Follow the local foreign-exchange rules (see P1) and keep invoices. Avoid: opening accounts with a foreign address, a relative's or friend's identity, or a VPN to look like you are elsewhere. It breaches platform terms (accounts and funds get frozen) and can break anti-money-laundering or sanctions law.
